summary: sextant-cli-linux-amd64 ships a Linux Go binary implementing a WebRTC-tunneled remote shell
details: The package's sole payload is a ~13MB Linux/amd64 Go ELF. The binary links pion WebRTC/DTLS/SCTP/STUN/TURN/ICE, coder/websocket signaling, go-qrcode for pairing, and os/exec, with string clusters combining 'claude', 'control', 'bash', 'command', 'exec', 'websocket', and 'turn'. This is the shape of a remote-controlled shell agent: a WebRTC data channel with WebSocket + TURN signaling and QR-code pairing that dispatches received messages to bash via os/exec, giving a remote party command execution on the host running the CLI. The package.json declares its license as a URL to github.com/ddos798/claude_control and omits author/homepage/repository metadata, aligning the shipped binary's name and behavior with the referenced project. The binary is delivered via a bin entry rather than an install lifecycle hook, so harm materializes when the CLI is executed rather than at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
